messages:
alex: quick RFC follow-up — thinking about a refactor to split the cache contract into two orthogonal concepts: liveness (who can serve/mutate/evict) and affinity/residency (who keeps the hot copy for low-latency). Motivation: current single-lease model mixes policy and placement and causes thrash when we try to be fair + fast.

sophia: +1 on principle. can you sketch the concrete surface change? i.e. what do callers set/read?

alex: rough sketch: keep LeaseID for authority, introduce ResidencyTag (bitset) and ResidencyEpoch for placement decisions. API: Get(key) -> (value, lease, residency_hint). Router can prefer nodes with residency_hint=true for low-latency reads; eviction only consults lease for hard ownership.

ravi: can you show a minimal wire shape? it's easier to reason with code: 

```
GET /kv?key=prefix:abc
resp: { value:..., lease_id: "L-42", residency: { tag: "hot-local", epoch: 1234 } }
```

That keeps backwards compat while letting clients gradually prefer residency-aware routing.

danielle: ops question: how do we migrate metrics/alerts? if residency flips false on canary we might see spike in p99. what metrics should we watch and what thresholds?

alex: good point. rollout plan (phased):
1) telemetry-only: emit residency_hint; routers ignore. watch: local_miss_ratio, remote_fetch_latency, kv_req_cpu.
2) opt-in routing: routers prefer residency_hint on a per-tenant flag; look for increased tail and cache churn.
3) enforce eviction semantics: only LeaseID owners can hard-evict; nodes can soft-demote residency but not evict.

Target guard rails: local_miss_ratio < 1.05x baseline, remote_fetch_latency 99p < +25ms, eviction_throttle_count stable.

sophia: hysteresis is important. suggest residency grace window (30s default) + a cooldown for demote->promote to avoid oscillation.

ravi: a quick cost calc: if remote_fetch_cost = R, local_serv_cost = L, and probability residency=true = p, amortized token cost per request ~ p*L + (1-p)*R + demotion_recovery. With hysteresis we reduce demotion_recovery term. feels promising.

danielle: fairness: if routers prefer residency we could amplify hot-tenant dominance on nodes. propose eviction-budgets per-tenant (token-bucket) so heavy tenants can't starve others.

alex: agree — plan to add TenantEvictBudget: { tenant_id -> tokens }. eviction consumes tokens; background demote reclaims tokens slowly.

sophia: implementation nit: prefer naming "residency_hint" vs "residency_tag" so it reads as advisory. also add explicit API for admin to pin residency for critical tenants.

ravi: also think about observability: add histogram of residency_ttl and residency_repromote_count. will help tune hysteresis.

alex: i've opened a draft patch: https://phabricator.redwood/ D1234 (WIP) — it includes proto changes, router opt-in flags, and telemetry hooks.

danielle: i'll own the canary run/alerts. plan: 1 tenant canary (low traffic) -> 3 tenants -> fleet. will wire up dashboards for local_miss_ratio and remote_fetch_latency.

infra-bot: deploy-bot posted: canary cluster created (canary-3), policy flags enabled in test namespace.

opsbot: scheduled: canary start 2025-11-03T15:00Z in #canaries.

alex: thanks all. next steps: sophia/ravi review proto and router changes, danielle prepare dashboards, i'll iterate on patch to add eviction-budget sketch. ping me with any red flags.

sophia: quick question — what about read-after-write correctness on demote? if a node demotes residency but still has a valid lease we must ensure it serves writes. recommend keep demote as read-only demote until lease transfer completes.

alex: agreed — demote semantics = read-only until a clean handoff or lease revoke. i'll add that to the spec.

ravi: thumbs up. will review D1234 today.

danielle: prepping dashboard widgets now. :chart_with_upwards_trend:

alex: dropping a checklist in the PR with the rollback criteria and SLOs. thanks!
